title: Reviving a sluggish sourdough starter
description: User is reviving a sluggish sourdough starter; Dorothy covered feeding ratios, the hungry acetone smell, and fridge storage between weekend bakes.
abstract: The user is reviving a sluggish sourdough starter and prefers brief answers. Dorothy recommended feeding every 12 hours at 1:2:2 by weight (e.g. 20g starter, 40g flour, 40g water), discarding first, keeping it at about 24-27°C, adding 20-50% whole wheat or rye, and using non-chlorinated water. It's ready when it reliably doubles in 4-8 hours. The user reported a nail polish remover smell; Dorothy said it means hunger, not spoilage, and suggested more frequent feeding or 1:3:3 or 1:5:5, whole grain, and slightly cooler temperatures. Discard it if it has pink or orange streaks or fuzzy mold; grayish hooch is fine. The user then asked about fridge storage, since they only bake on weekends. Dorothy advised chilling only once it's healthy, feeding weekly at 1:2:2 or 1:5:5, and giving one or two warm feedings 12-24 hours before baking. Left open: whether the smell faded, and the starter's age and flour.
